explanation: Maintain the best length and skip starts that cannot improve it. Check a prospective longer window backward; a nonincreasing pair rules out every start crossing that break. When the window passes, extend forward through the increasing run and retain its inclusive endpoints.
timeComplexity: O(n) comparisons amortized: backward checks skip the tested broken segment, and successful forward extension advances beyond the checked window. A simple scan visits each pair once; skip-based implementations amortize backward checks against skipped starts.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary state and one endpoint pair. Only indices, lengths and one best interval are retained.

correctness: A nonincreasing adjacent pair cannot lie inside any strictly increasing subarray, so skipping starts that would include that pair loses no improving solution. A window longer than the current best that passes the backward check is increasing; forward extension finds its maximal end. The scan thus discovers any run longer than the saved best and returns a maximum-length interval.
walkthrough: For [2,4,4,5,7], the first increasing run has indices (0,1), length 2. Equality between the 4s blocks any run crossing indices 1 and 2. The next run spans (2,4), length 3, so return those endpoints; the judge reports 3. The JSON expected value is the wrapper’s length, not the returned endpoint record.
edgeCases: Empty input returns endpoints (0,−1), whose observed length is 0.
For a nonempty decreasing array, return a one-entry interval.
